note: T40 measurement layer - DATA MODEL AND DECISION PLAN. This file is a proposal, not an implementation. It defines what could be measured on this site, what may be measured under the program rules, and what each measurement would let the owner decide - so that the choice in discovery/suggestions.html DS-11 can be made against a concrete design instead of an idea. NOTHING here collects anything today: there is no script, no endpoint, no cookie and no account. The `status` of every event is DESIGNED, never LIVE, and the measurement gate fails the build if that ever changes without a recorded owner decision.

principles.rule: No personal data, no cookie, no cross-site identifier, and no identifier derived from a visitor.
principles.why: Amazon's Participation Requirements forbid associating a sub-tag or reporting ID with a specific end user (R-08 in ledger/compliance.json; S02 in ledger/sources.json). A design that cannot do that even if asked is stronger than a policy that says not to.

principles.rule: Measure the page and the link, never the person.
principles.why: The only questions this site needs answered are 'which page sends people to which product' and 'which page earns'. Both are aggregate counts on a page-plus-link key. Nothing about an individual changes any decision the owner can make.

principles.rule: Publish no traffic, conversion or income expectation, and no forecast.
principles.why: The Operating Agreement states that Amazon makes no representation or warranty regarding the amount of traffic or commission income an Associate can expect (S57). A projection on this site would present as knowledge exactly what that clause disclaims. The layer records what happened; it never prints what will.

principles.rule: Every event has a stated decision it supports, or it is not collected.
principles.why: Measurement without a decision is cost with no benefit. This file therefore lists the decision beside each event, and the gate refuses an event with no decision.

principles.rule: Search measurement must not route visitors straight to Amazon.
principles.why: Search results, paid or unpaid, must send users to the site and not directly or indirectly to an Amazon Site (S50). Any Search Console or paid-search plan is constrained by that.

events.name: page_view
events.fires_on: A dashboard or marketing page being served.
fields: referrer_host ONLY (the hostname, never the full URL or query)
events.decides: Which pages are being found at all. This is the only event that would justify writing the next page.
events.analogy_in_repo: Nothing today. The repository has no client-side script beyond render functions in assets/js/app.js.

events.name: product_link_click
events.fires_on: A click on a product link, before navigation.
fields: product_key (P1/P2/P3 - a static label from the fact base, never a value derived from the visitor)
deliberately_not_collected: whether the visitor bought anything (the site cannot know this and must not imply it does)
events.decides: Which page and which product deserve more work. This is the single most useful measurement on an affiliate site.
events.analogy_in_repo: tools/link_builder.py already labels every link with data-link-state="PREVIEW_NO_TAG"; the event key exists in the markup today and simply nothing counts it.

events.name: disclosure_view
events.fires_on: The required disclosure entering the viewport above a product link.
events.decides: Whether the disclosure is actually in the reader's line of sight before the first product link, which is what the FTC guidance asks for (S54). This is a compliance measurement, not a marketing one.
events.analogy_in_repo: Every page already carries the sentence and the link-level tag; nothing verifies that a reader sees it before the first link.

events.name: conversion_import
events.fires_on: A manual or scheduled import of the Associates reporting CSV for a period.
deliberately_not_collected: any per-customer data - Associates reporting is aggregate by design
any value this project could compute but Amazon does not publish
events.decides: Whether any of the above converted, and therefore whether the whole content strategy is working.
events.blocked_by: DQ-01: no Associates account exists, so no reporting exists to import. The site must not invent a placeholder figure to fill this table.
events.analogy_in_repo: tools/validate_data.py already forbids a populated clicks/conversion/earnings field anywhere in ledger/. This event is the only route by which those fields could ever legally be filled.

events.name: search_query_import
events.fires_on: A periodic export from Search Console.
deliberately_not_collected: any query containing something that looks like a person's name or address (filtered at import)
events.decides: Which question people actually typed, which is the only reliable input to a content plan. Without it every new article topic stays a judgement.
events.blocked_by: DQ-04: Search Console requires the owner's Google account and a verified property.
events.analogy_in_repo: marketing/trending-topics.html already argues that no topic on this site can be called trending without data. This event is what would make that possible.

decisions_enabled.rule: A page with impressions and no clicks is a packaging problem; a page with clicks and no imports is a product-fit problem. The layer must be able to tell those apart, which is why EV-01 and EV-02 are separate events.

decisions_enabled.decision: Which of the three products to lead with
decisions_enabled.rule: Count product_link_click by product_key. The product with the most clicks on the least content is the one to write about next.

decisions_enabled.decision: Whether the disclosure is placed well enough
decisions_enabled.rule: If disclosure_view does not precede the first product_link_click on a majority of sessions, the layout is failing the FTC's 'hard to miss' standard and should change.

decisions_enabled.decision: Whether to change the content strategy at all
decisions_enabled.rule: Nothing above can answer this. It needs actual conversions, which need an account. Until then the honest answer to 'is this working' is 'unknown', and the site says so.

privacy_and_consent.position: A design that stores no personal data and sets no cookie has no consent banner problem under the usual cookie rules, because there is no cookie and no identifier. That is the main reason to prefer this design over a third-party analytics script (option B in DS-11).
privacy_and_consent.what_is_asserted: Only the design position above, which is this project's own engineering judgement.
privacy_and_consent.what_is_not_asserted: No claim is made about GDPR, CCPA or any specific jurisdiction's requirements, and none should be inferred from this file. Whether a cookie-free aggregate counter falls inside or outside a particular regime is a legal question the owner must put to their own adviser. Recorded as a gap, not an answer.

open_items.item: The event sink does not exist. GitHub Pages serves static files and cannot accept a POST, so a first-party counter needs an endpoint the owner controls (a serverless function, a log drain, or a hosted database).
Retention policy is undefined. Aggregate daily counts can be kept indefinitely; anything finer should expire. The owner must choose before collection starts.
A bot filter is undefined. A static counter counts crawlers and link scanners as visitors. Without a filter the numbers are inflated and the decisions built on them are wrong.
There is no way to verify a click led to a purchase from this side, and this project must never imply there is. Attribution is Amazon's to report, not this site's to guess.
